verdict: Caution: lend selectively to organised Thrissur manufacturers with tight gold-metal control; avoid unorganised job-work units.
title: Thrissur gold jewellery manufacturing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Thrissur gold unit buys bullion or scrap, converts it into 22-carat chains, bangles and studded pieces, and sells to retailers or through group showrooms.** Cash is tied up in metal, not in machines: the working-capital intensity of such manufacturers has stayed high at 15-20% and is likely to rise with gold prices [10]. Pricing power is thin because unorganised players and established peers limit flexibility [8]. So when a proposal lands, check the gold-metal-accounting policy first; if the unit holds unhedged stock beyond a week's production, ask for the hedging contract.

## What has changed now
**The local demand signal is positive but the credit signal is not.** Kerala GST collections grew 10.3% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], and Thrissur's anchor houses are expanding — Malabar Gold opened a new MG Road showroom with launch offers [1]. **Money is chasing this trade faster than the trade is growing.** Regulatory intervention has already hit demand and supply [10], and bullion-import restrictions remain a live risk [8].

## Where the growth is
**Pursue organised manufacturers supplying large retail chains, and the mid-carat story.** Peer results show the appetite: Shanti Gold's Q4 FY26 revenue grew 121.65% YoY with PAT up 465.30% [4], and Q3 FY26 revenue grew 110.06% [6]. Sky Gold's management notes 18-carat is taking share from 22-carat, though 22-carat still holds 70%-75% of sales [5]. Ashapuri's EBITA margin expanded 233 bps to 8.78% [7]. **Avoid pure job-work units with one buyer and no own design capability** — they carry the metal risk without the margin.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the metal, not the turnover.** Take the gold on consignment or hypothecation with a daily stock-and-ornament statement; set the drawing power on net metal position, not on receivables alone. Peer balance sheets show the template: NGJL ran Total Debt/Tangible Net Worth of 0.5 times with interest cover of 4.0 times in FY2025 [9]. **Every month take: metal stock statement, sales register by carat, buyer-wise receivables ageing, and GST returns.** If receivables days stretch beyond the unit's own stated cycle, ask for the buyer confirmation.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the metal account and the buyer list, not the P&L.** ICRA flags that working-capital utilisation stays high and liquidity improvement is the monitorable [11]. If a unit's limit utilisation stays pinned near sanctioned levels while sales fall, that is diversion. If a single retailer crosses a third of sales, ask for a second-buyer plan. If the unit cannot produce a hedging contract when gold prices rise, treat it as a trading position, not a manufacturing one.

## The call
**Caution.** Thrissur's local demand is real [1][D], but the national credit-to-output gap [D] and thin pricing power [8] mean we lend to organised, hedged, multi-buyer units only. Sources on Thrissur-specific manufacturer financials are thin — collect from customer.
watch: Stock age > 15 days or unhedged position -> freeze drawing power
Filing gap or turnover fall > 20% -> ask for buyer-wise sales register
